items.titleEn: Gold climbs above $4,050 as Wall Street rallies ahead of Fed decision - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were higher in late U.S. trading Tuesday, recovering from early-session losses as declining crude oil prices eased inflation concerns and supported renewed buying interest in precious metals ahead of Wednesday's Federal Reserve monetary policy decision. Diplomatic efforts involving Iran and several regional powers helped reduce some of the immediate geopolitical risk premium in energy markets, while stronger U.S. economic data and a firmer dollar limited bullion's advance. At the latest verified afternoon price reading, spot gold was trading near $4,058.20 an ounce, up $42.00, or 1.05%, while spot silver was trading near $54.200, up $0.353, or 0.66%, on the session. Tuesday's U.S. economic reports pointed to resilient consumer demand and business investment despite elevated borrowing costs. September durable goods orders rose 1.8%, following a modest increase in August, supported by stronger transportation equipment demand. Orders excluding transportation increased 0.5%, while nondefense capital goods orders excluding aircraft, a closely watched measure of business investment, also advanced 0.5%. October consumer confidence increased sharply to 91.7 from an upwardly revised 84.2 in September, exceeding market expectations. The present situation index climbed to 120.4, while the expectations index improved to 72.6, partially reversing three consecutive monthly declines. September new-home sales slipped to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 676,000 units from a revised 680,000 in August, although the result exceeded expectations of approximately 650,000. The Richmond Fed manufacturing index remained at minus 2 in October, indicating continued modest contraction in regional factory activity.

items.titleEn: Downside risks are building in gold, but prices still have a path to $5,000 - State Street's Doshi
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold 's struggle to hold support around $4,000 an ounce is testing investor confidence in the precious metal, but one major investment firm remains optimistic that prices can recover to $5,500 by early next year. However, persistent inflation, rising bond yields and a more hawkish Federal Reserve are making that bullish outlook increasingly uncertain. In its latest Monthly Gold Monitor, State Street Investment Management maintained its forecast for gold prices to trade between $4,750 and $5,500 an ounce by the end of the first quarter of 2027. However, the firm reduced the probability of that scenario to 60%, down from 70%, as higher interest rates and a stronger U.S. dollar continue to weigh on the non-yielding precious metal. The gold team, led by Aakash Doshi, Head of Gold Strategy at State Street, highlights growing uncertainty surrounding the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook, even as structural demand continues to support the broader gold market.

Gold price needs to build a floor here or face a deeper correction - Standard Chartered's Cooper
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold ’s drop below $4,000 last week is starting to attract some early attention as the two-month downtrend has pushed prices toward oversold territory. However, according to one market analyst, the precious metal needs to hold current levels or could see significantly lower prices. In her latest precious metals report, Suki Cooper, Global Head of Commodities Research at Standard Chartered Bank, noted that global gold-backed exchange-traded products (ETPs) saw renewed outflows late last week, ending a period of relatively resilient investment demand. “Notably, the sell-off extended beyond gold across assets, reflecting tech jitters and liquidity needs to meet margin calls or generate cash,” she said.
